seo.title: Demo: a real coaching session with Cairnly
seo.description: Scroll through a complete coaching session of a fictional candidate: where the candidate pushes back, what the coach does with it, and how the report changes. Real AI output, no script.

nav.label: Demo: a real coaching session
nav.honest: Demo account. Real analysis and responses.

marcel.tagline: Marcel, 41, customer service team lead at an insurer. Done managing a team, wants to be closer to the people he helps.

emma.tagline: Emma, 38, senior marketing manager at a London fintech. Can do the job with her eyes closed, and that is exactly the problem.

intro.title: A real coaching session, start to finish
intro.body: This is the conversation as {{name}} had it: the report arrives chapter by chapter, {{name}} reacts, the coach reacts back. Nothing was polished afterwards.
intro.watchLead: Watch for these moments along the way:
intro.legendAside: The numbered moments sit in the bar at the top; click a number to jump there. On the left you see the report sections, exactly as in a real session.
intro.howTo: Click the cards to open them, hover over the radar, and click the buttons under a career to see what {{name}} did with them. You cannot type here: this is a replay.

welcome.caption: Every session starts like this: the coach introduces itself, you click the button and the first chapter arrives. Go ahead and click, it jumps to the start of the conversation.
welcome.pillsCaption: Under every coach message you then get these four buttons. They steer the conversation: continue, dig deeper, push back, or bring up something else. Shown here for illustration, not clickable.

fallback.otherLanguage: This session was held in English: Emma is a British candidate. The buttons and labels follow your language, the conversation stays in English.

pushback.title: He disagrees
pushback.body: Marcel clicks 'I see this differently' and says exactly where the analysis goes too far. No form, no star rating: pushback in his own words.

kept.title: The coach takes it on board, and he keeps it
kept.body: The coach corrects the analysis on the spot. Marcel presses Keep and this answer goes into his final report word for word. That is how the report becomes his, not just about him.

pillTag.title: The little label above the text
pillTag.body: It shows which button Marcel pressed before he started typing, here 'Something else'. So the conversation shows how he steered, not just what he said.

movePill.title: One click, and the coach backs up its rating
movePill.body: Under every career sits a button with the step the report expects, here 'Ready now'. Marcel clicked it: the question above was written for him automatically and the coach explains why no retraining is needed. Click that button on any career card and you jump here.

radar.title: Three careers, five axes, no template
radar.body: This radar is drawn from his own scores. Hover over a name to see that career on its own, and click 'Explain this comparison' to read what the difference means for him.

askRole.title: He aims his question at one career
askRole.body: Every career card has 'Ask about this role'. Marcel used it on Facilitator Restorative Practices: his message gets the [About …] label and the coach answers about that career only. Click that button on any card and you jump here.

dictated.title: He did not type this, he said it
dictated.body: Marcel dictated this answer through the microphone. Speech recognition turns it into text and the AI tidies it up (stumbles, repetitions, punctuation) before he presses send. What you read is his story, just neater.

pushback.title: She disagrees
pushback.body: Emma clicks 'I see this differently' and draws the line herself: the loop is fair, the 'late scramble' is not her. No form, no star rating: pushback in her own words, and the coach rewrites its reading on the spot.

kept.title: She keeps it, and it lands in her report
kept.body: The coach reframes her fintech years as more scope, less proximity to the story. Emma presses Keep and this answer goes into her final report word for word. That is how the report becomes hers, not just about her.

pillTag.title: The little label above the text
pillTag.body: It shows which button Emma pressed before she started typing, here 'Something else'. She brings in two things the survey never asked about: a promotion decision due this quarter and her partner's shift rota. Watch the coach carry both into the career chapter.

movePill.title: One click, and the coach defends its rating
movePill.body: Under every career sits a button with the step the report expects, here 'Upskill'. Emma clicked it: the question above was written for her automatically and the coach explains why this is not 'Reframe' and not 'Retrain' either. Click that button on any career card and you jump here.

radar.title: Three careers, five axes, no template
radar.body: This radar is drawn from her own scores. Hover over a name to see that career on its own, and click 'Explain this comparison' to read what the difference means for her. Emma read it and told the coach the radar was being kind to number two.

askRole.title: She aims her question at one career
askRole.body: Every career card has 'Ask about this role'. Emma used it on Design Sprint Facilitator, the only card rated 'Ready now': her message gets the [About …] label, the coach answers about that career only, and concedes that it is a business, not a job. Click that button on any card and you jump here.

dictated.title: She did not type this, she said it
dictated.body: Emma dictated this answer through the microphone. Speech recognition turns it into text and the AI tidies it up (stumbles, repetitions, punctuation) before she presses send. What you read is her story, just neater.

highlights.title: What this conversation changed in the report
highlights.body: At wrap-up the coach summarises the session. These points now sit in {{name}}'s report, next to the answers kept along the way.
